statement: enforcer-coordination (arc-16, already landed) has NO mail/message API yet — only init/claim/release/closeout exist in crates/enforcer-coordination/src/api.rs. The L21 lesson (mail ignores lane param for sender identity) therefore cannot be fixed by the MCP tool layer alone: this crate's router registers coordination_mail/coordination_message tool NAMES (for tools/list surface parity + the d05 measure) but dispatches them as 'registered but not yet wired' rather than fabricating a working handler.
why: A worker reading only the workpack's L21 requirement text could wrongly assume the MCP surface must itself re-implement mail semantics; the actual fix belongs in enforcer-coordination's own future mail module, and this MCP layer's job is to not regress/mask that gap by faking success.
howToApply: When a workpack says 'the coordination-tool defects... MUST NOT exist in your Rust MCP surface where it wraps arc-16', first check whether the underlying arc-16 crate actually exposes the verb at all. If it doesn't, the correct action at the MCP layer is an honest not-yet-wired response, not a local reimplementation that would fork the fix away from its owning crate.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-mcp/src/router.rs dispatch() default arm; crates/enforcer-coordination/src/api.rs (no mail module)

statement: The workspace [workspace.lints] clippy deny wall (unwrap_used/expect_used/panic) is NOT relaxed inside #[cfg(test)] modules in this workspace's rustfmt/clippy config — every test that would normally use .expect("...") or panic!(...) must instead return Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> and use `?`, or use `let ... else { unreachable!() }` (unreachable! is NOT in the deny set, unlike panic!/todo!/unimplemented!).
why: Several sibling crates' test modules (enforcer-config) already establish the Result-returning-test pattern, but it is easy to default to .expect()/panic! out of habit when writing NEW fixture-style tests (this pass hit 13 clippy errors from exactly this before fixing).
howToApply: When writing tests in this workspace, default every #[test] fn to `-> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` with `?` on fallible calls; reach for `let X = ... else { unreachable!("...") }` only when destructuring an enum variant that has no natural `?` conversion.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-mcp/src/{transport,sink,router,registry}.rs test modules; cargo clippy -p enforcer-mcp --all-targets pre-fix output (13 errors: panic/expect_used)

statement: The legacy .mjs MCP dogfood scanner (ocentra_enforcer_scan/check via the frozen worktree) applies the ocentra-parent hardened dependency-justification/domain-brand posture uniformly to EVERY crate in this workspace when invoked with an ad hoc `files` scope, including already-landed/accepted sibling crates (confirmed: crates/enforcer-harness/src/query.rs scanned in isolation produces the same RR-9.18/RR-9.3/RR-1.5/RR-6.x class of findings as a fresh new crate). This is scanner-profile noise, not a defect specific to a new pack.
why: A worker seeing 50+ 'violations' against their own new crate could wrongly conclude their crate is uniquely non-compliant and over-fix (e.g. adding DEPENDENCY-JUSTIFICATION comments nowhere else in the workspace) when the correct read is 'the legacy scanner's files-scope invocation is stricter than the posture actually gating landed work'.
howToApply: Before treating a legacy-scanner dogfood finding as real, spot-check the SAME ruleId against an already-landed, already-accepted sibling crate via the identical scan invocation shape; if the sibling shows the same finding class, it is scanner-profile noise (verbatim-summarize per protocol), not a new defect to chase.

evidence.ref: ocentra_enforcer_scan files=[crates/enforcer-mcp/src/router.rs] vs files=[crates/enforcer-harness/src/query.rs] — both produce RR-9.18/RR-9.3/RR-1.5/RR-6.x on their own Cargo.toml
